"Is this an insult to Kinnera Mogulaiah, or an insult to the Padma Shri?"

Padma Shri awardee and Kinnera artist Darshanam Mogulaiah has once again had to knock on the doors of officials regarding the housing plot allotted to him by the government. In 2022, the then Telangana government had allocated a 600-square-yard housing plot in Kuntlur to him, along with a cash prize of ₹1 crore.

In September 2024, Chief Minister Revanth Reddy personally handed over the land allotment documents. However, Mogulaiah states that he has not yet received the final housing *patta* (title deed) and has not even gained proper possession of the land, as it is entangled in court disputes and other issues.

Furthermore, the Hayathnagar police registered a case after unidentified individuals demolished the compound wall constructed on the site in October 2024. Mogulaiah mentioned that he has been making rounds of government offices and courts for two years regarding this land and has incurred a debt of approximately ₹9 lakh for lawyer fees and court expenses. On June 22, Mogulaiah attended the 'Praja Vani' (public grievance) program at the Ranga Reddy Collectorate and submitted a representation to District Collector C. Narayana Reddy, requesting the immediate issuance of the title deed and the resolution of the issues surrounding the land. He expressed his anguish, noting that while other awardees had received their title deeds, he could not understand why his case remained pending. He also stated that if the issue remains unresolved, he would meet Chief Minister Revanth Reddy directly to seek justice.

The way the Collector treated Kinnera Mogulaiah during the 'Praja Vani' (public grievance redressal) program is now drawing severe criticism. There is a prevailing sentiment that the artist—honored by the nation with the Padma Shri—was not accorded even basic courtesy; the Padma Shri is a prestigious civilian award conferred by the Government of India for "distinguished service."
When a Padma Shri awardee approaches a Collector to present a grievance, listening respectfully and responding appropriately are the minimum standards the public expects from the administration.
Critics argue that this incident appears to belittle not just Mogulaiah as an individual, but also the honor of the Padma Shri bestowed upon him by the nation.
Artists deserve to be treated with respect not only when being felicitated on stage but also when they visit government offices to address their grievances.

Criticism has arisen regarding the lack of due respect shown to Kinnera artist Mogulaiah—honored by the nation with the Padma Shri—when he visited the 'Praja Vani' program to address an issue concerning his house site. Objections have been raised over the Collector failing to stand up to welcome him or even offering him a seat. There is a strong view that basic courtesy should have been extended to a folk artist of national repute when he met the official to discuss his problem.
This also raises the question of how officials treat recipients of national awards. The fact that Mogulaiah has to stand and present a formal grievance to resolve his land issue is causing dissatisfaction among many.

“Kinnera Mogulaiah met the Collector in June and requested a resolution to his problem; he was assured that the matter would be settled soon. However, by the end of September, the dispute regarding the land allocated to him remained unresolved, and the issue concerning the land title deed (patta) persisted. Although the government announced new measures in September to address pending land disputes across the state, there is no reliable information yet indicating that Mogulaiah’s personal case has been settled. The fact that a folk artist honored with the Padma Shri has to wait for months to secure his rights over government-allocated land is now becoming a major issue of concern.”

🚨 Binance P2P se Bank Account Freeze? Poori Guide + Real Solution (2026)

Bhai aur beheno, agar aap bhi Binance P2P trading karte ho aur suddenly bank account freeze ho gaya hai toh pareshan mat ho. Yeh bahut common problem hai India mein. Innocent log bhi fas jaate hain jab kisi buyer/seller ka paisa kisi fraud case se link hota hai.

Yeh steps follow karo - 

1️⃣ Sabse Pehle Bank Branch Jaao  
   - Freeze ka exact reason, Cyber Crime complaint number, IO naam aur Police Station details lo.  
   - Written notice maang lo.

2️⃣ Saare Proofs Collect Karo (Bahut Important)  
   - Binance P2P complete order history (screenshots)  
   - Buyer/Seller ke saath chat  
   - Payment proof (UPI, bank transfer screenshot)  
   - Bank statement jisme transaction dikhe  
   - Aadhaar, PAN, Binance account details

3️⃣ Binance Support ko turant contact karo  
   - App mein Help section → Submit ticket  
   - Order ID aur proofs attach karo. Woh counterparty ko investigate kar sakte hain.

4️⃣ Cyber Cell mein Representation Daalo  
   - Local Cyber Police Station ya online portal pe jaao.  
   - Detailed application likho ki transaction genuine tha Binance P2P pe hua.  
   - Saare proofs attach karo.  
   - Lawyer (Cyber crime specialist) ki madad le lo - yeh bahut kaam aata hai.

5️⃣ Follow-up karte raho  
   - Har 7-10 din mein bank aur cyber cell ko call/email karo.  
   - Partial release ke liye request kar sakte ho.

Extra Tips jo future mein bacha sakte hain:
• P2P ke liye alag dedicated bank account use karo (savings account mat use karo)
• Sirf verified buyers/sellers ke saath trade karo

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

is the ECI compromised?  
 In March 2026, ahead of the Kerala Assembly elections (polling on 9 April 2026), a 2019 Election Commission of India (ECI) letter redistributed by the Kerala Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office was found to carry the seal of the BJP’s Kerala unit. This sparked a political row, followed by police-directed efforts to remove related social media posts

This takedown action itself became controversial, with critics framing it as an attempt to suppress discussion of an official lapse during an election period, while authorities maintained it was necessary to stop the circulation of a withdrawn and erroneous document that was being used to question the ECI’s credibility.The episode remained a flashpoint in the final stretch of the Kerala campaign, with the ECI treating it as a corrected administrative mistake and the opposition presenting it as evidence of deeper concerns about the poll body’s independence.The letter and the seal
The document was an ECI communication dated 19 March 2019 containing guidelines/FAQs on the publicity of candidates’ criminal antecedents (following a Supreme Court judgment). CPI(M) and Congress shared versions online showing the BJP Kerala unit’s seal. It had been circulated by the Kerala CEO’s office to political parties, District Election Officers, and Returning Officers as part of clarifications around mid-March 2026.thesouthfirst.comKerala CEO / ECI explanation:
It was described as a “purely clerical error.” The BJP Kerala unit had approached the CEO’s office seeking clarification on the (by then revised) 2019 guidelines and submitted a photocopy of the original directive that already bore the party’s seal. Staff overlooked this and redistributed that version. The error was identified; on 21 March a formal withdrawal notice was issued telling recipients to disregard the document. An Assistant Section Officer was suspended pending inquiry. Later, a Deputy CEO and a Section Officer were relieved of election-related duties.livemint.comOpposition parties (CPI(M) and Congress) rejected the clerical-error account. They alleged compromised institutional neutrality, claiming seals were being “casually swapped” and questioning whether the ECI and BJP shared the same “power centre.” Some BJP responses labelled the circulation of the old document as misinformation or a political plot.thewire.inDeletion of posts controversyActing on an ECI directive (under the Model Code of Conduct), the Kerala Police cyber cell issued notices to X (Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, and numerous individual accounts. They demanded removal of posts sharing the letter that carried the BJP seal.  Police argued the content insulted the Election Commission, undermined its integrity and transparency, spread false claims about a rectified clerical error, and risked public order or communal harmony by potentially fuelling political division. Reports indicated hundreds of accounts were flagged (approximately 270 on X, 200 on Facebook, and 90 on Instagram). Facebook and Instagram largely complied; X forwarded the notices to users, some of whom then posted the notices themselves. Journalists and political commentators also received
